text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 3 in history.
1789 - Claude-Joseph Vernet, French painter known for his seascapes, died.
1800 - In the War of the Second Coalition, the French defeated the Austrians at the Battle of Hohenlinden in upper Bavaria.
1810 - Britain seized the islands of Reunion and Mauritius from French control.
1818 - Illinois became the 21st state of the United States.
1823 - Giovanni Battisti Belzoni, Italian explorer and excavator of Egyptian archaeological sites, died.
1857 - Joseph Conrad, Polish-born British novelist, born; among his best known works are "Lord Jim" and "Nostromo".
1883 - Austrian composer Anton von Webern born; his music was banned by the Nazis in World War Two and he was accidentally shot and killed by a U.S. soldier in 1945.
1884 - Indian statesman Rajendra Prasad born; he became first president of the Republic of India in 1950.
1894 - Robert Louis Stevenson, Scottish author of "Treasure Island", died.
1910 - The neon lamp, developed by French physicist Georges Claude, was displayed for the first time at the Paris Motor Show.
1919 - French impressionist painter Pierre Auguste Renoir died; his painting of sunlight through leaves and a series of pictures portraying bathers are amongst his best-known works.
1923 - Maria Callas, U.S.-born operatic soprano, born; she changed the world of opera with her ability to act out roles on stage which had previously been just sung.
1930 - French film director Jean Luc Godard born.
1931 - The Statute of Westminster was passed, under which British dominions gained complete legislative independence.
1967 - Dr Christiaan Barnard carried out the world's first heart transplant operation in Cape Town on Louis Washkansky. Washkansky lived for 18 days.
1969 - Kliment Voroshilov, former head of the presidium of the Supreme Soviet, died.
1971 - The Pakistani air force attacked Indian airfields and Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi declared a state of emergency.
1980 - Oswald Mosley, leader of the British Union of Fascists before the Second World War, died.
1984 - A gas leak at the Union Carbide pesticide plant near Bhopal, India, killed nearly 4,500 people.
1989 - Presidents Bush and Gorbachev hailed their first summit as the start of a new era in U.S.-Soviet relations.
1989 - The leader of East Germany's orthodox Communist Party, Egon Krenz, and the entire party hierarchy voted themselves out of office.
1990 - Rebel soldiers captured army headquarters in central Buenos Aires and seized part of a suburban infantry garrison in a short-lived bloody dawn mutiny.
1993 - Angola's government and its rebel foes agreed to a ceasefire in their 18-year war.
1993 - Princess Diana said she was bowing out of the public spotlight because she wanted privacy and time to herself.
1994 - In Georgia, gunmen shot dead Georgy Chanturia, head of the moderate opposition National Democratic Party.
1995 - U.S. President Bill Clinton ordered 700 American troops to be deployed in Bosnia as part of an advance NATO peacekeeping force.
1995 - Former South Korean president Chun Doo Hwan was arrested over charges of military rebellion stemming from a 1979 coup and a later army massacre.
